title: Application Security & Defensive Engineering
summary: Production security guidelines to protect APIs and frontend apps against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.
keyPrinciples: Never trust client input: validate and sanitize all incoming payloads at the boundary.
Principle of Least Privilege: services and database users should only have the minimum required permissions.
Defense in depth: rely on multiple overlapping security controls rather than a single perimeter check.

rules.title: Always Scope Database Queries to the Authenticated Tenant/User
rules.description: Prevent Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA/IDOR) by forcing the query to filter on user/tenant ownership, rather than trusting raw URL parameters.

badExample.explanation: The server fails to check if the requesting user actually owns the invoice.

goodExample.explanation: The database query enforces tenant isolation at the data access layer.

rules.title: Never Inject Secrets Directly Into Source Code or Git Repositories
rules.description: Hardcoded API keys, database credentials, or signing secrets in git commit history will be leaked. Load them from environment secrets managers at runtime.

badExample.explanation: Once committed to git, credentials remain in git history even after deletion.

goodExample.explanation: Secrets are loaded dynamically and validated strictly on process boot.

productionChecklist: Automated secret scanning (Gitleaks, TruffleHog) in CI/CD pipeline.
Strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP) headers enabled on all web responses.
All user inputs validated with strict schemas (Zod, Pydantic, or JSON Schema).
Authentication tokens stored in HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax cookies.
